execution_steps: 1. Read model/document.py's cited source and Python's own zipfile module source (inspect.getsource) to confirm exactly how ZIP member filenames are decoded: filename.decode('utf-8') with no error handling when the UTF-8 filename flag (0x800) is set, meaning invalid UTF-8 bytes in a UTF-8-flagged entry raise UnicodeDecodeError during ZipFile construction.

2. Confirmed OraContainer.from_bytes() only catches zipfile.BadZipFile, not UnicodeDecodeError -- meaning a malformed-Unicode member name would currently crash with a raw stdlib exception type rather than the package's own OraArchiveError, violating the obligation's 'reject ... before payload use' requirement via an unhandled crash rather than a clean, typed rejection.

3. zipfile's own writer API (ZipFile.writestr, ZipInfo) only ever accepts a valid Python str for a filename, so no test using it could ever construct an invalid-UTF-8 name. Hand-built a minimal ZIP byte-for-byte with struct.pack (local file header + central directory record + end-of-central-directory record) carrying an explicitly invalid UTF-8 byte sequence as the filename, with the UTF-8 flag bit set, and confirmed interactively that zipfile.ZipFile() raises UnicodeDecodeError on it before writing any fix.

4. Added an except UnicodeDecodeError clause around the zipfile.ZipFile() construction in from_bytes(), converting it into a clean OraArchiveError, and verified interactively that the fix produces the correct, typed error.

5. Wrote test_malformed_unicode_member_names_are_rejected using the same hand-built-ZIP technique as a reusable helper (_archive_with_raw_member_name), and ran it plus the full container test file and full ora suite before writing any evidence claim.

6. Separately, re-swept ora's remaining unresolved obligations for stale or reusable citations from this session's earlier ticks. Found SAL-ORA-OBL-2BFD0DF67723D491 (ORA-BASELINEASSET-001) carries the identical 'full baseline support for reading and editing and viewing... editing may damage the result' rule_text already resolved for 4 other obligations at event 175 via the LOSSLESS-vs-CANONICAL PreservationMode evidence -- closed via the same cross-capability citation reuse, zero new code. Found SAL-ORA-OBL-96D74D42B49F8C8B (ORA-GROUP-001)'s missing_behavior claiming 'root restrictions... not tested' was stale: event 175 already added test_an_image_with_no_root_stack_is_refused and test_an_image_with_multiple_root_stacks_is_refused to test_obligation_stack_and_document.py, but they had never been cited against this specific obligation. Added them, keeping the obligation honestly partial since its other 2 findings (composite-op open vocabulary, unknown-extension preservation) remain genuine, unresolved gaps.

7. Ran ruff and mypy on the one changed source file (clean), the full ora suite (289 passed, was 288), ran the skills-first resolve/manifest/receipt/closeout sequence since src/ was touched, then patched the evidence YAML and ran the reconciler.
